prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Stronger Economy, Fairer Society: Opportunity for Everyone

The Liberal Democrats set out a five‑year plan for an open, optimistic, outward‑looking UK that combines sound finances with social justice, green growth and equal rights.

Responsible finances and fair taxes
- Balance the structural current budget by 2017/18 with a fair mix of savings and taxes on wealth, big banks and polluters; debt to fall year on year thereafter.
- No rises in headline Income Tax, NI, VAT or Corporation Tax; raise the Personal Allowance to at least £12,500; clamp down on avoidance and non‑dom status; levy on high‑value property.

Prosperity for all: a high‑skill, low‑carbon economy
- Long‑term Industrial Strategy; double economy‑wide R&D; expand apprenticeships and National Colleges; devolve economic levers locally.
- Reform finance: stronger British Business Bank; more competition, community and alternative finance.
- Green leadership: Zero Carbon Britain by 2050; expand the Green Investment Bank; end unabated coal by 2025; set a 2030 power decarbonisation target with up to 60% renewables; back community energy; tight fracking rules with revenues funding the transition.
- Modern infrastructure: HS2 as part of a UK‑wide network, rail electrification, city‑region transport, clean air zones, ultra‑low‑emission vehicle rollout, near‑universal high‑speed broadband.
- Open, trading nation: stay in a reformed EU, complete the Single Market, support fair trade deals, welcome talent and students.

Real help for families and work
- Expand free childcare to 20 hours for ages 2–4 and from nine months for working parents, complete Tax‑Free Childcare.
- Make work pay through Universal Credit; protect disability benefits; promote flexible work and Shared Parental Leave; transparency to close the gender pay gap; Living Wage in central government.
- Pensions: make the Triple Lock permanent; continue auto‑enrolment; fairer, simpler savings.

World‑class education, cradle to college
- Protect funding from nursery to 19; strengthen the Pupil Premium; qualified teachers in every class.
- End child illiteracy and innumeracy by 2025; a slim core curriculum including PSHE, financial literacy and age‑appropriate SRE; independent standards body.
- Double firms hiring apprentices; improve FE; widen university access and protect income‑contingent finance; discount bus travel for 16–21s.

Health, care and wellbeing
- Invest at least £8bn extra a year in England’s NHS by 2020; integrate health and social care; improve GP access.
- Parity for mental health with waiting‑time standards and a £500m uplift; better children’s and perinatal services; crisis care that ends use of police cells.
- Support carers with a £250 annual bonus and new rights; cap care costs; raise care quality.
- Public health first: curb junk food marketing to children, tobacco levy, proportionate e‑cig rules, minimum alcohol pricing, cleaner air and warmer homes.

Homes and greener places
- Build 300,000 homes a year with Garden Cities, public‑land development and a Housing Investment Bank.
- Boost affordable housing; “Rent to Own” and Help to Rent; stronger tenant protections.
- Green Buildings Act: upgrade homes to EPC Band C (fuel‑poor by 2027); council tax discount for major efficiency improvements.
- Five Green Laws: Nature, Zero Carbon, Green Transport, Resource Efficiency/Zero Waste, and Green Buildings; expand accessible green space and protect wildlife; support sustainable farming and fair food chains.

Freedom, justice and secure communities
- Protect the Human Rights Act; pass a Digital Bill of Rights; a second Freedoms Act; evidence‑led policing with local Police Boards; a Victims’ Bill of Rights.
- Tackle violence against women and girls; rehabilitate offenders with smart non‑custodial sentences; health‑led drug policy.
- Restore full entry/exit checks; fair, efficient asylum; welcome skilled migrants and students.

Power to people and nations
- Home Rule within a federal UK; a Constitutional Convention; votes at 16; proportional representation (STV) for Commons and local government; reformed Lords; cap big money in politics; devolution on demand in England.

Britain in the world
- Lead in the EU, NATO, UN and Commonwealth; support a safe, reformed EU; climate leadership (EU −50% by 2030; zero‑carbon UK by 2050); step down nuclear posture while maintaining security; keep aid at 0.7%; champion human rights and LGBT+ equality worldwide.
